extracted.intended_audience: students and professional mathematicians who will use the Magma computer algebra system
extracted.subtask_description: An introductory manual describing the Magma programming language, its user environment, and the implemented algebraic/categories functionality; aimed at teaching users how to write and run Magma code and how to use its algebraic data types and functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: What Is Magma? (purpose and design)
rubrics_metrics.description: Magma is a programming language designed for the investigation of algebraic, geometric and combinatorial structures, or magmas. The syntax of the language resembles that of many well-known programming languages. What is special about Magma is the provision of mathematical data types such as groups, rings, fields, sets, sequences and mappings, together with a large collection of functions for performing standard tasks in algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information about the magmas and their elements is stored in a mathematically powerful way, making advanced symbolic algebraic computation feasible. Magma is a sophisticated tool for experimentation, education, and computer-aided proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended users and uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Magma is useful for both students and professional mathematicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is presented as a tool for experimentation, education, and computer-aided proof — i.e., appropriate for learning, research experimentation, and assisting rigorous mathematical work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book prerequisites and pedagogical approach
rubrics_metrics.description: This book is an introductory manual for Magma. It presumes no knowledge of computer programming, and its examples are chosen to illustrate language and algorithmic features as simply as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Volume I explains the language and user environment in detail, and Volume II deals with the major algebraic, geometrical and combinatorial structures implemented in the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation and recommended further reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Note carefully that this book does not attempt to give comprehensive coverage of the algorithms implemented in Magma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before undertaking serious computations in Magma, the user should also consult the reference manual, Handbook of Magma Functions (referred to within the book as Handbook).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative short introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Although this book is designed as an introduction, the short booklet First Steps in Magma may be more appropriate for those requiring only a passing acquaintance with the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: System versioning and update guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The version of the system documented in this edition is Magma V2, released in 1996.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release notes for later versions may be obtained from the developers of Magma (i.e., users should check for and consult release notes when using newer versions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics / competency areas covered (table of contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: The manual enumerates the core topics a user should learn: getting started; creating structures and elements; language basics (expressions, identifiers, assignment, conditional and iterative statements); aggregate structures (sets, sequences, lists, tuples); mappings/homomorphisms; functions and procedures; intrinsics, signatures and packages; the user interface and online help; strings, printing and I/O; files and processes; user environment; and extensive algebraic areas (rings and fields, polynomial rings, finite fields, number fields, modules and algebras, groups, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These chapter headings indicate the required knowledge/skills and the functional areas supported by Magma; learners should use the corresponding chapters to acquire competency in those areas (e.g., 'Warning About Large Magmas' signals performance considerations; 'Online Help' and 'Intrinsics, Signatures and Packages' indicate where to find built-in functionality).
